record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For n = 14 and for all n >= 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph on n vertices with maximal energy the graph P_n^{6;6}, obtained from two 6-cycles and a path P_(n-12) by attaching each path endpoint to one of the cycles by a single edge? Here a molecular graph means a connected graph of maximum degree at most 4.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.9 For n = 14 and n >= 16, the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximal energy is the molecular graph of the alpha, beta diphenyl-polyene C6H5(CH)n-12C6H5, which is represented by the graph P6;6_n obtained from two copies of the cycle C6 and a path Pn-12 by attaching with an edge each endpoint of the path to on cycle (see Fig. 6).

The complete solution, in that case, was given by Huo et al. (2011). Theorem 5.10 Let G be any connected, bipartite bicyclic graph on n >= 12 vertices. Then E(G) <= E(P6;6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6;6_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The energy of a finite simple graph $G$ with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ is $E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n |\lambda_i|$. A molecular graph is a connected graph in which every vertex has degree at most 4. A bicyclic graph is a connected graph with exactly $n$ vertices and $n+1$ edges. For integers $n\ge 14$, let $P_n^{6;6}$ denote the graph obtained from two disjoint copies of the 6-cycle $C_6$ and a path $P_{n-12}$ on $n-12$ vertices by joining each endpoint of the path to a single vertex of one of the two 6-cycles (one endpoint to each 6-cycle) via an additional edge.

Prove or disprove: for $n=14$ and for every integer $n\ge 16$, among all bicyclic molecular graphs on $n$ vertices the unique graph attaining the maximum energy is $P_n^{6;6}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been fully resolved for connected bipartite bicyclic graphs on n ≥ 12 vertices (Huo, Li, Shi, 2011), where the maximum energy graph is indeed P_n^{6;6}. For the non-bipartite case (bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles, including molecular bicyclic graphs that need not be bipartite), the conjecture remains open in general, although numerical computations verify it up to n = 50.

status_evidence.title: Solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of bipartite bicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Huo, Li, Shi prove that P_n^{6,6} has maximum energy among bipartite bicyclic graphs for n ≥ 12.

status_evidence.title: Maximum energy bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles with one common vertex
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture remains open for bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles; partial results exist for special subclasses.
